meaning.name: Browse a category
meaning.statement: When a visitor opens a category, the shop shall list its products four to a page, sorted by one of five orders, with filters by price, stock and rating beside the list and numbered pages under it.

meaning.says: Given a category of six products, when it is opened, then four products are listed with their name, stars, count of reviews, price, stock state and Add to cart, the page says "Showing 1–4 of 6 products", and page 2 holds the other two.
Given the list, when a sort order is chosen and applied, then the same products are listed in that order.
Given the list, when a page's number, Previous or Next is selected, then that page opens and is marked as the one open.
Given a filter ticked and applied, when the list is shown again, then only the products that match it are listed.

meaning.name: Sign out
meaning.statement: When a customer selects Sign out in the account menu, the shop shall end their session, keep their cart for the next sign-in, and say so.

meaning.says: Given a signed-in customer, when Sign out is selected, then the page says "You are signed out" and "Your cart is kept for the next time you sign in.", and the header shows Sign in and Sign up.
Given a cart of two lines at sign-out, when the customer signs in again, then the cart holds the two lines.

meaning.name: Keep the profile
meaning.statement: When a customer opens their profile, the shop shall show their name, email, phone and delivery address to change, a way to change the password, and a way to delete the account.

meaning.says: Given a signed-in customer, when Profile is opened, then the fields hold what the account has, and Save changes writes what was changed.
Given the current password and a new one, when Change the password is selected, then the new one signs the customer in from then on.
Given a field refused, when Save changes is selected, then the field says why and nothing is changed.

meaning.name: Follow my orders
meaning.statement: When a customer opens My orders, the shop shall list their orders with the number, date, count of items, total and status, and open each to its lines, its steps from placed to delivered and its delivery address, with Cancel this order while it is still placed.

meaning.says: Given a customer with four orders, when My orders opens, then the four are listed, each leading to its page.
Given a placed order, when it opens, then the four steps show Placed as the one reached and Cancel this order is offered.
Given a shipped order, when it opens, then Shipped is the step reached and no Cancel is offered.
Given another customer's order number, when its address is opened, then the shop answers as for an order that does not exist.

meaning.name: Move an order as the admin
meaning.statement: When the admin opens the orders, the shop shall list every customer's order with the customer's email under the filters All, Open, Shipped and Cancelled with their counts, find one by number or email, and on an order offer the moves its status allows and a note to add.

meaning.says: Given eight orders, when the admin opens Orders, then "All (8)" is chosen and the eight are listed with the customer's email; "Open (3)" lists the placed and the paid, "Shipped (4)" the shipped and the delivered, "Cancelled (1)" the cancelled.

Given a placed order, when the admin opens it, then Mark as paid and Cancel the order are offered; given a paid one, then Mark as shipped and Cancel the order; given a shipped one, then Mark as delivered; given a delivered or a cancelled one, then nothing.
Given a move the status does not allow, when it is asked of the shop, then it is refused and the order is unchanged.
Given a note typed, when Add is selected, then the note is kept on the order with who added it and when.

meaning.name: Only the staff reach the admin
meaning.statement: When someone who is not the admin opens a page or a call of the admin's part, the shop shall refuse it: a page that says the part is for the staff, with a way back to the shop, and 403 for a call.

meaning.says: Given a customer who is not the admin, when /admin/orders is opened, then the page says "This part of the shop is for its staff. You are signed in as a customer." and offers Back to the shop.
Given a visitor, when /admin/orders is opened, then sign in comes first.
Given a customer's session, when an order is moved by the call, then the answer is 403 and the order is unchanged.

meaning.name: A wishlist
meaning.statement: When a customer selects Save for later on a product, the shop shall keep it in a list of their own, to buy another time.

meaning.name: A page for an address the shop does not have
meaning.statement: When anyone opens an address the shop does not have, the shop shall show a page of its own, in the shop's frame, that says so and offers the home page and the search.

meaning.says: Given an address no page has, when it is opened, then the page shows the shop's header and footer, says that there is no page at that address, and offers the home page and the search.
Given the address of a product that no longer exists, when it is opened, then the same page shows.

meaning.name: See a product
meaning.statement: When a visitor opens a product, the shop shall show its name, its stars and count of reviews, its SKU, its price with the old price and a Deal mark where it has one, its stock state, a line about it, its specifications, its reviews, the three promises and three more products.

meaning.says: Given a product with a deal, when its page opens, then the price, the old price struck out and the word Deal show together.
Given a product with three or fewer left, when its page opens, then the low-stock words show in place of "In stock".
Given a product out of stock, when its page opens, then "Out of stock" shows, Add to cart is disabled, and the page offers to tell the customer when it is back.
Given an address of a product that does not exist, when it is opened, then the shop answers that no product has that slug.

meaning.name: Search the products
meaning.statement: When anyone types words in the search and sends it, the shop shall list the products whose name or description holds the words, say how many match, and say when nothing does.

meaning.says: Given the word "headphones", when the search is sent, then the page says "5 products match." and lists the five as a category does.
Given words no product holds, when the search is sent, then the page says "Nothing matches." and "Check the spelling, try fewer words, or browse a category.", and offers the popular searches.
Given the home page, when a popular search is selected, then the search's results for that word open.

meaning.name: Add a product to the cart
meaning.statement: When a visitor or a customer selects Add to cart on a product in stock, the shop shall add it to their cart in the quantity chosen, one to five, or raise the line's quantity where the product is in the cart already.

meaning.says: Given a product in stock and a quantity of 2, when Add to cart is selected, then the cart holds a line of that product with quantity 2 and the header's count rises by 2.
Given the product is in the cart with quantity 4, when 2 more are added, then the shop refuses it with "up to five of each product" and the cart is unchanged.
Given a product out of stock, when the cart is asked to add it, then the shop refuses it and the cart is unchanged.
Given a visitor's cart, when they sign in, then the cart is theirs under the account.

meaning.name: Change the cart
meaning.statement: When a visitor or a customer opens the cart, the shop shall show each line with its product, price, quantity and total, let them change a quantity or remove a line, take a discount code, and show the subtotal, the delivery and the total.

meaning.says: Given a cart of two lines, when it opens, then each line shows the product, its price, a quantity with a minus and a plus, its total and Remove, and the summary shows the subtotal, the delivery and the total.
Given a line of quantity 1, when its minus is selected, then the line is removed.
Given a subtotal of €377.00, when the cart opens, then the delivery is "Free"; given a subtotal of €39.00, then the delivery is €4.90.
Given a code, when Apply is selected, then the summary shows what the code takes off, or the field says that the code is not known.
Given an empty cart, when it opens, then the page says "Your cart is empty." and offers to start shopping.

meaning.name: Check out and place an order
meaning.statement: When a customer selects Checkout with a cart that holds a line, the shop shall ask for the delivery address and one of three ways to pay, show the total, and on Place order make the order from the cart, placed.

meaning.says: Given a signed-in customer with a cart, when Checkout is selected, then the checkout shows the name, the street and number, the city and the postcode, each required, and Card, PayPal and Invoice with Card chosen.
Given the address filled and a way to pay chosen, when Place order is selected, then an order is made with the cart's lines, the address and the total, in the status placed, and the cart is emptied.
Given a required field empty, when Place order is selected, then the field is marked and no order is made.
Given a line out of stock since it was added, when Place order is selected, then the shop refuses the order and says which line.
Given a visitor, when Checkout is selected, then sign in comes first, and the checkout after it with the same cart.

meaning.name: Sign in
meaning.statement: When a visitor sends their email and password, the shop shall sign them in to their account, keep them signed in on the device where they ask it, and refuse a wrong pair above the form with both fields marked and what was typed kept.

meaning.says: Given an account's email and password, when Sign in is selected, then the customer is signed in and the header greets them by name.
Given a wrong email or password, when Sign in is selected, then the page says "The email or the password is wrong." above the form, both fields are marked, and what was typed stays.
Given Keep me signed in ticked, when the browser is closed and opened again, then the customer is still signed in.

meaning.name: Create an account
meaning.statement: When a visitor sends their name, email, a password typed twice and the terms accepted, the shop shall make their account and sign them in, and refuse a form with a field wrong by saying how many need a look above it and why under each.

meaning.says: Given a name, an email no account has, a password of eight characters with a number typed twice and the terms ticked, when Create account is selected, then the account is made and the customer is signed in.

Given "ana@" as the email, a password of five letters and a repeat that differs, when Create account is selected, then the page says "Three things need a look." above the form, and under the fields "That is not an email address.", "At least 8 characters, with a number." and "The two passwords differ."
Given the terms not ticked, when Create account is selected, then the form is refused and nothing is made.

meaning.name: Recover the password
meaning.statement: When a visitor sends their email on the password page, the shop shall send a link to choose a new password where an account has that email, and say the same on the page after whether or not one does.

meaning.says: Given an account's email, when Send the link is selected, then the page says "If an account has that address, a link is on its way. It works for one hour." and the email holds a link.
Given an email no account has, when Send the link is selected, then the page says the same and nothing is sent.
Given a link an hour old, when it is opened, then it no longer works.

meaning.assumptions: - The shop's counter of abandoned checkouts counts the same thing on the new platform. To check: run both counters on the same week before the old shop is switched off, and compare. - The orders placed by phone are counted by the warehouse, by hand, and will go on being counted the same way. To check: ask Lea for the count of the first week after launch.
meaning.journey: 1. A visitor arrives at the home page, or at a product from a search engine, and browses a category or searches. 2. They open a product, read its price, its stock and its reviews, and add it to the cart. 3. In the cart they change the quantities, apply a code where they have one, and go to the checkout; signed out, they sign in or create an account first. 4. At the checkout they give the delivery address, choose a way to pay, and place the order; today this is where the site most often stops them, and they phone. 5. Under My orders they follow the order from placed to delivered, and cancel it while it is still placed. 6. In the warehouse the admin marks the order paid, shipped and delivered, with a note where one is needed.
meaning.name: Voltline
meaning.non-goals: - A wishlist, reviews written on the site, and gift cards: the owner says no to each every year, and the move is not the moment (E4). - Anything the shop does not do today: the move adds nothing and loses nothing (E1). - The warehouse's own tools beyond the admin's orders: the shop ends at the order's status.
meaning.problem: The shop is being moved to a new platform and nothing of what the customer sees is to change; without a specification the new team would read the old code and guess. Today about 12 orders a week are placed by phone because something on the site stopped the customer, most often at the checkout, and 68 of every 100 checkouts started are abandoned, by the shop's own counter in September 2026 (E2, E3). The owner lays the slowness behind both at the platform's door, and the move is meant to cure it without changing the shop.

meaning.summary: Voltline is a small electronics shop on the web: a catalogue of six categories, a cart, a checkout with three ways to pay, an account with its orders, and an admin's view of every order. This specification says what the shop does today, screen by screen and call by call, so that the team moving it to a new platform in the spring of 2027 builds the same shop (E1).
meaning.users: The visitor: anyone who browses the catalogue, searches, and fills a cart without an account (U1). The customer: a visitor with an account, who buys, sees their orders and keeps their details; today they are stopped by the site about 12 times a week and phone the shop instead (U2). The admin: the two people in the warehouse, who move each order along from placed to delivered, or cancel it (U3). Each is a customer too, signed in to the same account.
